about: DXY, also known as DingXiang Doctor, is a Hangzhou-based Chinese online healthcare platform and doctor community founded in 2000, with a professional network of millions of physicians, a consumer health information site (Dingxiang Yisheng), an online pharmacy, and medical education and recruitment services. Revenue comes from pharma marketing, e-commerce and health services. Backed by Tencent and other major investors. Strong recognition among Chinese doctors and a large consumer health audience.

AVEO Pharmaceuticals was a Boston oncology biopharma, listed on Nasdaq (AVEO), that developed Fotivda (tivozanib), approved in the US and Europe for advanced kidney cancer. It sold to oncologists through specialty pharmacies and licensed rights in Europe. LG Chem acquired AVEO in early 2023 for about 566 million dollars. B2B pharma brand with no consumer profile. Fotivda was approved by the FDA in March 2021 for relapsed or refractory renal cell carcinoma after prior therapies.

CareDx is a Brisbane, California diagnostics company, listed on Nasdaq (CDNA), selling AlloSure, AlloMap and HistoMap tests that monitor organ transplant patients for rejection using blood tests, with transplant centres as customers. Revenue is about 300 million dollars with Medicare as a key payer. Founded in 1998. Specialist clinical diagnostics brand known among transplant doctors, with little public awareness. It also sells software and services for transplant centres, and competes with Natera in donor-derived cell-free DNA testing.

ChemoCentryx was a San Carlos, California biopharma, listed on Nasdaq (CCXI), that developed Tavneos (avacopan), approved for ANCA-associated vasculitis, an autoimmune kidney and blood vessel disease, licensed to Kyowa Kirin and CSL Vifor. Amgen acquired it in 2022 for about 3.7 billion dollars. Customers are nephrologists and rheumatologists. Pharma-sector brand with no consumer profile. Tavneos was approved by the FDA in October 2021, and the company earned royalties and milestone payments from its partners.

Insitro is a South San Francisco machine-learning-driven drug discovery company founded in 2018 by Daphne Koller, using cell models, human genetics and large datasets to find treatments, with collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb and Eli Lilly. Funded by Andreessen Horowitz, Third Rock and others. Customers are pharma partners paying milestone and research fees. B2B biotech with a high profile in AI-in-biotech circles but no consumer awareness.

Kadmon Corporation was a New York biopharmaceutical company, listed on the NYSE (KDMN), that developed Rezurock (belumosudil), the first FDA-approved treatment for chronic graft-versus-host disease. Sanofi acquired it in 2021 for about 1.9 billion dollars. Customers were transplant specialists. B2B pharma brand with no consumer profile. Founded in 2010 by Harlan Weisman, it was financed by venture investors and public markets, and had previously focused on other immunology and fibrosis assets.

Mersana Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq (MRSN), developing antibody-drug conjugates using its Dolaflexin and Immunosynthen platforms, with collaborations including Takeda and GSK. It has no marketed products and earns revenue from partnership payments. Cancer therapies are its focus. B2B biotech with no consumer profile. Founded in 2011 with Flagship Pioneering backing, its candidate emiltatug ledadotin (XMT-1660) targets B7-H4 on solid tumours.

Theravance Biopharma is a South San Francisco biotech, listed on Nasdaq (TBPH), with a royalty interest in Trelegy Ellipta and Breo Ellipta (sold by GSK), and a focus on clinical-stage drugs such as ampreloxetine for neurogenic orthostatic hypotension in multiple system atrophy. Revenue comes mainly from royalties and partnerships, and it sold Vibativ in 2022. B2B pharma brand with no consumer profile.

Affimed is a Mannheim, Germany clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq (AFMD), developing innate cell engager (ICE) antibody therapies that direct natural killer cells against cancer, including AFM13 for lymphoma. Revenue comes from collaborations with Roche, Genentech and Artiva. It has no commercial products. B2B biotech with no consumer profile. It has research and development operations in Heidelberg and Mannheim and a pipeline that also includes AFM24 for solid tumours.

Azenta Life Sciences, formerly Brooks Automation, is a Burlington, Massachusetts company, listed on Nasdaq (AZTA), providing sample management services, cold-chain storage, genomics (Genewiz) and multiomics services to pharma, biotech and academic researchers. It sold its semiconductor automation business in 2021 to Thomas H. Lee Partners. Revenue is around 600 million dollars. B2B life-science brand with no consumer awareness. Its Genewiz unit performs DNA sequencing and gene synthesis for researchers, and B Medical Systems makes cold-chain refrigeration for vaccines and blood.

Biofourmis is a Boston-based digital health company, founded in Singapore in 2015, selling an AI platform with wearable biosensors that tracks patients at home after hospital care and flags deterioration early, plus digital therapeutics for pharma. Customers are hospitals, health plans and drugmakers. Backed by SoftBank and others at a valuation above 1 billion dollars. It merged with CopilotIQ in 2023 to create Biofourmis Care, later renamed Biofourmis. B2B healthcare technology firm with little public awareness.

Dice Therapeutics was a South San Francisco clinical-stage biotech developing oral small-molecule drugs for immunology, using its DELSCAPE platform to target integrins. Its lead candidate DC-806 was an oral IL-17 inhibitor for psoriasis. Eli Lilly acquired it in 2023 for about 2.4 billion dollars. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer profile. Founded in 2013, the company listed on Nasdaq (DICE) in 2021 before the Lilly acquisition, using its platform to find oral alternatives to injected antibodies.

DNAnexus is a Mountain View, California cloud platform for genomic and biomedical data, used by pharma, hospitals and public health bodies to store, analyse and share sequencing data under compliance controls, with customers including the US FDA and national precision-medicine programmes. Revenue comes from platform and service fees. Founded in 2009 and backed by GV, Foxconn, Eight Roads and others. B2B bioinformatics brand known in genomics circles.

Knight Therapeutics is a Montreal-based specialty pharmaceutical company, listed on the TSX (GUD), that in-licenses, acquires and distributes branded and generic medicines in Canada and Latin America, and invests in innovative pharma assets. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and public payers across Canada and Latin America. Revenue is around 350 million Canadian dollars. B2B pharmaceutical firm with little consumer recognition. It also distributes through Latin American subsidiaries in Brazil, Argentina, Colombia and Mexico, and invests in funds that back healthcare start-ups.

Quanterix is a Billerica, Massachusetts life sciences company, listed on Nasdaq (QTRX), whose Simoa digital immunoassay technology detects proteins at very low concentrations, used in neurology research, Alzheimer's blood tests and drug development. It sells instruments, assays and services to academic and pharma researchers and acquired Akoya Biosciences in 2025. Revenue is about 130 million dollars. B2B brand known in research labs, not consumer-facing.

Reify Health is a Boston-based healthcare technology company with cloud software for running clinical trials, including StudyTeam for site operations and patient recruitment, used by pharma sponsors, contract research organisations and trial sites. Backed by Founders Fund and Silver Lake at a 2 billion dollar valuation. Revenue comes from software subscriptions. Layoffs followed in 2023. B2B life sciences software brand known to clinical operations teams.

Sierra Oncology was a San Mateo, California clinical-stage oncology company, listed on Nasdaq (SRRA), that developed momelotinib for myelofibrosis, a bone marrow cancer. GSK acquired it in 2022 for about 1.9 billion dollars, and momelotinib was approved in 2023 as Ojjaara. Customers were haematologists. Pharma-only brand with no consumer profile. Momelotinib treats myelofibrosis patients with anaemia, a subgroup that other drugs can worsen, and Sierra licensed it from Gilead in 2018.

Athenex was a Buffalo, New York biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (ATNX), that made oncology drugs including Klisyri (tirbanibulin) for actinic keratosis and had a generic injectables and API manufacturing business in China and the US. Losses led to Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023, and assets were sold. Customers were dermatologists and hospitals. B2B pharma brand with no consumer profile.

CinCor Pharma was a Boston clinical-stage cardiovascular biotech, listed on Nasdaq (CINC), developing baxdrostat, a selective aldosterone synthase inhibitor for resistant hypertension. AstraZeneca acquired it in 2023 for up to 1.8 billion dollars. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer awareness. The company was built around a licence from Roche, and its Phase 2 data in resistant hypertension drew the AstraZeneca bid, followed by Phase 3 trials.

Jubilant Pharma is the pharmaceutical arm of India's Jubilant Bhartia Group, with a US presence at Yardley, Pennsylvania. It runs radiopharmacies, contract development and manufacturing (Jubilant HollisterStier allergy products and Jubilant Radiopharma), generics and active ingredients, serving hospitals, pharma and drug distributors. Revenue is over 1 billion dollars. Parent Jubilant is listed in India. B2B pharma supplier with niche brand recognition.

Marinus Pharmaceuticals was a Radnor, Pennsylvania and Branford, Connecticut biotech, listed on Nasdaq (MRNS), that sold Ztalmy (ganaxolone), approved for seizures in CDKL5 deficiency disorder, a rare epilepsy. Revenue came from the sale to neurologists via specialty pharmacies. Struggling finances led to its acquisition by Immedica Pharma in 2025. B2B pharma brand with no consumer profile. Ztalmy was approved by the FDA in March 2022, and ganaxolone was later tested for status epilepticus in a trial that failed in 2024.

Quotient Biodiagnostics was a Newtown, Pennsylvania and Edinburgh-based diagnostics company, listed on Nasdaq (QTNT), developing the MosaiQ platform for blood grouping and transfusion testing, with customers in hospitals and blood banks. It struggled with debt and filed for Chapter 11 in 2023. B2B medical diagnostics brand with no consumer profile. MosaiQ is a microarray-based automated system designed to replace manual blood typing, and the company also sold reagents to blood banks.

RayzeBio was a San Diego clinical-stage biotech developing radiopharmaceutical cancer therapies that deliver radioactive isotopes such as actinium-225 to tumours using targeting molecules, with lead candidate RYZ101. It listed on Nasdaq (RYZB) in 2023 and was acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb in early 2024 for about 4.1 billion dollars. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer profile. RYZ101 targets somatostatin receptor-positive tumours such as gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours with actinium-225, and the company raised funds before listing.

Standard BioTools, formerly Fluidigm, is a South San Francisco life science tools company, listed on Nasdaq (LAB), selling mass cytometry (CyTOF), microfluidics and proteomics instruments and reagents to academic, pharma and clinical researchers. It merged with SomaLogic in 2024 and sells the SomaScan proteomics platform. Revenue is about 170 million dollars. B2B research tools brand known in labs but not by consumers.

VectivBio was a Basel-based clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq (VECT), developing apraglutide, a long-acting GLP-2 analogue for short bowel syndrome patients dependent on intravenous nutrition. Ironwood Pharmaceuticals acquired it in 2023 for about 1 billion dollars. Pre-revenue rare disease developer with no consumer profile. It listed on Nasdaq in 2021, employed fewer than 100 people, and its lead drug had completed a pivotal Phase 3 trial before the Ironwood deal.

Avistone Pharmaceuticals is a Beijing-based clinical-stage biotech developing targeted cancer therapies, including vebreltinib, a MET inhibitor licensed with Apollomics, and other kinase inhibitors for non-small cell lung cancer. It is private and funded by Chinese and international investors. No marketed products at the time. B2B pharma developer with no consumer profile. Vebreltinib has been approved in China for MET exon 14 skipping lung cancer, and the company has further kinase inhibitors in development.

BioRay Pharmaceutical is a biopharmaceutical company based in Taizhou, Jiangsu, China, per Crunchbase, in biopharma and biotechnology. It states it is committed to delivering life-changing medicines, which points to drug development, but the input does not confirm its products, pipeline or customers. Funding of about 2.5 billion yuan was recorded in January 2023. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Inozyme Pharma was a Boston clinical-stage rare disease biotech, listed on Nasdaq (INZY), developing INZ-701, an enzyme replacement therapy for ENPP1 deficiency and ABCC6 deficiency, which cause calcification and bone disorders. BioMarin agreed to acquire it in 2025. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer profile and not relevant to consumer sponsorship. Its ENPP1 deficiency indications include generalised arterial calcification of infancy and autosomal recessive hypophosphataemic rickets type 2.

PhenomeX was a Emeryville, California life sciences tools company formed in 2023 by the merger of Berkeley Lights and IsoPlexis, selling Beacon and IsoLight single-cell analysis platforms to pharma and academic labs for antibody and cell therapy discovery. It listed on Nasdaq (CELL) and was acquired by Bruker in 2023 for about 600 million dollars. B2B research tools brand with no consumer profile.

Selecta Biosciences was a Watertown, Massachusetts biotech, listed on Nasdaq (SELB), developing ImmTOR tolerogenic nanoparticles to prevent anti-drug antibodies, notably SEL-212 for chronic refractory gout, licensed to Sobi. It merged with Cartesian Therapeutics in 2023 and renamed itself Cartesian Therapeutics, now focused on mRNA CAR-T cell therapy for autoimmune disease. B2B biotech with no consumer profile. ImmTOR is combined with pegadricase for gout in Sobi-funded Phase 3 trials, while Cartesian now develops Descartes-08 for myasthenia gravis.

Thrive Earlier Detection was a Cambridge, Massachusetts cancer screening company that developed CancerSEEK, a multi-cancer blood test combining DNA mutations and protein biomarkers, developed with Johns Hopkins researchers and backed by Third Rock and Casdin. Exact Sciences acquired it in January 2021 for about 2.15 billion dollars. Customers were physicians and health systems. B2B diagnostics brand that is now part of Exact.

Ventus Therapeutics is a Waltham, Massachusetts and South San Francisco biotech developing oral small molecule drugs for inflammatory diseases, notably NLRP3 inhibitors for cardiovascular and neurological conditions, using structure-based computational design. It has a partnership with Novartis, which paid an upfront sum in 2022, and is venture-backed. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer profile. Its candidates also include a brain-penetrant NLRP3 inhibitor for neurological conditions and a cGAS inhibitor for lupus.

2seventy bio was a Cambridge, Massachusetts cell therapy company spun out of bluebird bio in 2021, listed on Nasdaq (TYO), which co-commercialised Abecma, a BCMA CAR-T therapy for multiple myeloma, with Bristol Myers Squibb. Bristol Myers Squibb acquired it in 2025 for about 286 million dollars. Customers were cancer centres. B2B biotech with no consumer profile. It also kept bluebird's oncology pipeline, including an anti-BCMA CAR-T programme and a Phase 3 trial in earlier-line myeloma.

Amolyt Pharma was a Lyon-area French biotech, based in Ecully, developing eneboparatide for hypoparathyroidism and other peptides for endocrine and rare diseases. AstraZeneca's Alexion unit acquired it in 2024 for up to 1.05 billion dollars. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer profile. Eneboparatide is a once-daily injected parathyroid hormone analogue in Phase 3, and Amolyt was founded in 2011 in the Lyon area.

Amphastar Pharmaceuticals is a Rancho Cucamonga, California specialty pharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (AMPH), making and selling injectables and inhalation products, including enoxaparin, Primatene Mist (an over-the-counter asthma inhaler), naloxone, glucagon, epinephrine and insulin products. It sells to hospitals, wholesalers and pharmacies, with revenue of roughly 700 million dollars. Primatene Mist gives it some consumer recognition in the US. It manufactures in California and China, and added Baqsimi nasal glucagon, bought from Eli Lilly in 2023, to its US insulin and emergency medicine range.

Bluepha is a Beijing synthetic biology and materials company founded in 2016, producing PHA (polyhydroxyalkanoates), a family of biodegradable plastics made by microbial fermentation, as well as other bio-based materials such as ingredients for personal care. Customers are packaging, consumer goods and textile brands, and it runs large fermentation capacity in China. Venture-backed with a large round in 2023. B2B materials firm with growing industry awareness and no consumer brand.

CanSino Biologics is a Tianjin-based Chinese vaccine company, listed in Hong Kong (6185) and on Shanghai's STAR Market, best known for Convidecia, a single-dose adenovirus-vector COVID-19 vaccine developed with the Academy of Military Medical Sciences, and for meningococcal conjugate vaccines such as Menhycia. It sells to national and provincial disease control centres and also supplies partners abroad. Founded in 2009. B2B vaccine maker with high profile in China during the pandemic.

Caribou Biosciences is a Berkeley, California clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq (CRBU), co-founded by CRISPR pioneer Jennifer Doudna, developing off-the-shelf allogeneic CAR-T cell therapies for blood cancers using chromosome-engineered cells, with candidates such as CB-010 for lymphoma. Revenue is limited to collaboration income, including partnerships with AbbVie and Pfizer. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile. Founded in 2011 by Doudna, Rachel Haurwitz and others, it uses chromosome editing to improve persistence of its CAR-T cells.

Hookipa Pharma is a New York-based clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq (HOOK), developing arenavirus-based immunotherapies against cancer and infectious diseases, including HB-200 for HPV16-positive head and neck cancer, partnered with Gilead in an HIV programme. It has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile. Founded in 2011 as a spin-out from Austrian research, its lead HB-200 combines two arenaviruses in a prime-boost regimen.

Lyndra Therapeutics is a Watertown, Massachusetts biotech founded from MIT research, developing ultra-long-acting oral capsules that release medicines over days to a week from a star-shaped structure in the stomach, to improve adherence for conditions such as schizophrenia and malaria. It partners with pharma companies and is venture-backed. Pre-commercial B2B firm with no consumer profile. Its LYN-005 candidate is a once-weekly risperidone capsule for schizophrenia in clinical trials, designed to improve adherence.

ReNAgade Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech, launched by Flagship Pioneering, building an RNA and delivery platform for programmable medicines, including mRNA and gene-editing therapies delivered to tissues beyond the liver. Funded with a 300 million dollar launch round and other venture investment, it is pre-commercial and works through partnerships. Developer for pharma customers with no consumer profile and little public awareness.

about: Sangon Biotech is a Shanghai-based Chinese life sciences supplier of molecular biology reagents, custom DNA oligos, gene synthesis, DNA sequencing and protein services, selling through catalogues and online to universities, research institutes and pharma labs across China. Founded in 1998 and one of the country's larger reagent suppliers. Revenue comes from product sales and services. B2B laboratory brand known to researchers, with no consumer profile.

Synthekine is a Menlo Park, California biotech developing engineered cytokine therapies that direct immune signalling, using synthetic cytokine receptors to treat cancer and autoimmune diseases, with partners including Roche. Venture-backed with late-stage private funding rounds. Pre-commercial B2B drug developer with no consumer profile. Its lead candidate STK-012 is an alpha/beta-biased IL-2 for solid tumours, and it collaborates with Roche. It has also raised money from major life-science investors.

about: Unity Biotechnology is a South San Francisco biotech, listed on Nasdaq (UBX), that developed senolytic drugs to clear senescent cells for age-related diseases, with a lead programme in eye disease, UBX1325, for diabetic macular oedema. Co-founded by Nathaniel David and backed by Amazon's Jeff Bezos among investors. It wound down in 2025 after trial results. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with some interest in longevity circles.

VYNE Therapeutics, formerly Menlo Therapeutics after its merger with Foamix Pharmaceuticals, is a Bridgewater, New Jersey biotech listed on Nasdaq (VYNE). It sold topical dermatology products such as Amzeeq and Zilxi, then sold them to Journey Medical in 2022 and refocused on BET inhibitors for immuno-inflammatory diseases. Small-cap specialty pharma that is now a clinical-stage developer with limited public awareness.

Acepodia is an Alameda, California clinical-stage biotech developing antibody-cell conjugation, which attaches antibodies to the surface of immune cells such as gamma delta T and NK cells to create off-the-shelf cancer therapies without genetic engineering. It was founded in Taiwan and is venture-backed. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. Its ACE platform conjugates antibodies to cells such as NK and gamma delta T cells, with programmes in blood cancers and solid tumours.

about: Aeglea BioTherapeutics was an Austin, Texas clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq (AGLE), that developed engineered enzymes for rare metabolic diseases, including pegzilarginase for arginase 1 deficiency. In 2023 it restructured and renamed itself Spyre Therapeutics, now a Waltham company developing antibodies for inflammatory bowel disease. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile. After the rename it moved to a Waltham base and combined with antibody programmes assembled by Paragon Biosciences.

AmplifyBio is a West Jefferson, Ohio contract development and testing organisation for cell and gene therapies, providing preclinical safety and efficacy studies, GMP manufacturing, analytical development and clinical-stage services to biotech clients. Its Ohio campus was built for advanced therapy development, with additional capabilities elsewhere in the US. Revenue comes from service fees from developers. Venture-backed B2B life sciences services brand with no consumer profile.

about: Black Diamond Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts precision oncology company, listed on Nasdaq (BDTX), developing MasterKey therapies against families of oncogenic mutations in EGFR and HER2, with lead candidate silevertinib in glioblastoma and lung cancer. It has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile. Founded in 2014 and listed on Nasdaq in 2019, it uses the Maverick computational platform to find drugs against grouped oncogenic mutations.

Boundless Bio is a San Diego precision oncology company, listed on Nasdaq (BOLD), developing therapies against tumours driven by extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), with candidates such as BBI-355, a CHK1 inhibitor, and BBI-825. It has no marketed products and relies on equity funding. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile. It listed on Nasdaq in 2024 after being founded in San Diego in 2018 around the biology of extrachromosomal DNA.

CardioFocus is a Marlborough, Massachusetts medical device company that makes the HeartLight endoscopic ablation system, a laser balloon catheter used to treat atrial fibrillation with direct visualisation of the heart tissue. It sells to hospitals and electrophysiologists in the US and Europe and is venture-funded. B2B medtech brand known among cardiologists, with no consumer profile. The HeartLight system received FDA approval in 2016 and has been used in hospitals in the US and Europe.

Chroma Medicine was a Boston epigenetic editing biotech, founded in 2021 by Nessan Bermingham and backed by Flagship Pioneering, developing technology that switches genes on and off without changing DNA. In 2024 it merged with Nvelop Therapeutics to form nChroma Bio. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. It launched with a large Series A in 2021 and aimed to treat disease by silencing genes through chemical marks on DNA rather than cutting it.

Eurofarma is a Brazilian multinational pharmaceutical company, based in Itapevi near Sao Paulo, one of Brazil's largest, selling prescription, generic and over-the-counter medicines, plus consumer health and dermocosmetics, in Brazil and across Latin America, with a growing US presence. It was founded in 1972, is privately held by the Lazar family, and has around 10,000 staff. Consumer health brands give it good awareness in Brazil.

Harpoon Therapeutics was a South San Francisco biotech, listed on Nasdaq (HARP), developing TriTAC T-cell engagers for cancer, including HPN328 for small cell lung cancer, with AbbVie as a partner. Merck acquired it in early 2024 for about 680 million dollars. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile. The company was founded in 2015, and its HPN328 candidate targets DLL3 in small cell lung cancer.

Mariana Oncology was a Watertown, Massachusetts radiopharmaceutical biotech founded in 2021, developing targeted radioligand therapies for cancer, backed by Dimension, Pfizer Ventures and others. Novartis acquired it in 2024 for up to 1 billion dollars. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. Its lead technology uses precision-targeted radioligands carrying lutetium-177 and actinium-225, and it began clinical work shortly before the Novartis deal.

Mural Oncology is a Waltham, Massachusetts biotech spun out of Alkermes in 2023 and listed on Nasdaq (MURA), developing nemvaleukin alfa, an engineered interleukin-2 therapy for ovarian cancer. After a disappointing late-stage trial in 2024 it moved to wind down its programmes. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile. Alkermes shareholders received Mural shares in the spin-off, and the company started with more than 275 million dollars in cash.

Omega Therapeutics was a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech, listed on Nasdaq (OMGA), founded by Flagship Pioneering, developing epigenomic controllers to programme gene expression for cancer and other diseases. It entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy in early 2025 after financing difficulties. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. Its OTX-2002 programme targeted MYC in hepatocellular carcinoma, and the bankruptcy left investors with little recovery.

Orbital Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech developing circular RNA and in vivo cell therapy treatments, aimed at autoimmune diseases and cancer using novel RNA technology with lipid delivery. It was launched in 2022 with Atlas Venture and Dimension investment, and Bristol Myers Squibb agreed to acquire it in 2025 for about 1.5 billion dollars. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Recro Pharma was a Malvern, Pennsylvania pharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (REPH), that ran a contract development and manufacturing business for drug makers and developed Anjeso, an injectable pain drug. It renamed itself Societal CDMO in 2022 and was acquired by CoreRx in 2024. B2B pharma services brand with no consumer profile. Its Gainesville, Georgia and Athens sites made solid dose products for pharma customers.

Relievant Medsystems is a Minneapolis medical device company that makes the Intracept system, which uses radiofrequency ablation of the basivertebral nerve inside vertebrae to treat chronic vertebrogenic low back pain. It sells to spine surgeons and pain physicians, with Medicare coverage. Boston Scientific agreed to acquire it in 2024 for about 850 million dollars. B2B medtech brand with no consumer profile.

Ring Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech launched by Flagship Pioneering, working on anelloviruses, harmless human viruses, as vectors for delivering gene therapies and redosable genetic medicines. It is venture-backed and pre-commercial, with a large funding round in 2023. B2B developer for pharma and patients, with no consumer profile. Its work focuses on a family of viruses called anelloviruses that exist in nearly every person without causing disease.

about: Septerna is a South San Francisco biotech, listed on Nasdaq (SEPN) since 2024, building a platform for discovering oral small-molecule drugs against GPCR drug targets, with partnerships with Novo Nordisk, Vertex and Otsuka and lead programmes in endocrine conditions such as hypoparathyroidism. Revenue comes from collaborations. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile. It was founded in 2019 on a Native Complex platform that makes GPCR proteins in a cell-free format for drug screening.

SinoTau Pharmaceutical is a Beijing-based Chinese company, classified in biotechnology and health care, which describes itself as a total solution provider in the field of radiopharmaceuticals for diagnosis and therapy, including PET tracers and nuclear medicine products. It sells to hospitals and imaging centres in China and raised a 1.98 billion yuan round in 2023. B2B healthcare firm with no consumer profile.

about: Stemirna Therapeutics is a Shanghai biotech focused on mRNA technology, developing mRNA drugs and vaccines, including a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine candidate, with lipid nanoparticle delivery and a production base in Shanghai. Founded in 2016, it raised about 1.7 billion yuan in 2023 from Chinese investors. Pre-commercial or early-stage B2B pharma developer with no consumer profile. It runs an mRNA vaccine and drug manufacturing facility in Shanghai and partners with Chinese and global biotechs.

Tessa Therapeutics is a Singapore biotech developing cell therapies for cancer, mainly an EBV-specific CD30 CAR-T treatment for relapsed lymphoma and virus-specific T-cell therapies, with trials in Asia and the US. Founded in 2011, it is venture-backed and runs a manufacturing facility in Singapore. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. Its CD30 CAR-T candidate TT11 has been trialled in lymphoma in Singapore and the US.

Vapotherm is an Exeter, New Hampshire medical device company that makes high velocity nasal insufflation systems, Precision Flow and Vapotherm Oxygen Assist Module, delivering heated, humidified respiratory support to patients with breathing difficulty in hospitals, emergency care and home care. It was listed on the NYSE (VAPO) and was taken private in 2024 by lender Perceptive Advisors. B2B medtech brand with strong recognition among respiratory therapists.

10 Biotech is a clinical-stage biotech company based in Copenhagen, Denmark, per Crunchbase, in biotechnology and health care. The description is cut off after saying it is developing therapies, and the input does not confirm its pipeline, indications or ownership. A funding round of about 242 million dollars is recorded in September 2025. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Acrivon Therapeutics is a Watertown and Cambridge, Massachusetts oncology biotech, listed on Nasdaq (ACRV), using its AP3 proteomics platform to match drugs to patients' tumours, with lead candidate ACR-368, a CHK1/2 inhibitor for endometrial and ovarian cancers. It has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile. Its drug candidates are directed by the AP3 platform, which analyses phosphoproteomics data on patient tumour samples.

Agile Therapeutics is a Princeton, New Jersey women's health company, listed on Nasdaq (AGRX), that sells Twirla, a weekly contraceptive skin patch, to women in the US through prescriptions, with telehealth and retail pharmacy channels. Revenue is small, around 20 million dollars, and the company has repeatedly raised funds. Consumer-facing prescription brand with limited public awareness. Corium manufactures the Twirla patch for the company, which struggled to scale prescriptions after the 2020 launch.

Alira Health is a Framingham, Massachusetts international advisory and consulting firm for the healthcare and life sciences industry, offering clinical research, regulatory, market access, digital health and strategy services to medtech, pharma and digital health clients, plus its Alira Health clinical research subsidiaries. It has offices across the US, Europe and Asia. Revenue comes from fees. B2B consultancy with brand recognition in the health industry only.

Alterome Therapeutics is a San Diego precision oncology biotech developing targeted small-molecule drugs, including AKT inhibitors for cancers with specific mutations, such as breast cancer, built by a team with prior kinase drug development experience. It has raised venture funding from institutional investors. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. It works from San Diego with a small research team and has disclosed few programme details beyond AKT-targeted oncology.

about: Bluejay Therapeutics is a privately held South San Francisco biopharmaceutical company developing antibody treatments for chronic hepatitis D and other liver diseases, with a lead candidate in clinical trials. It is backed by venture investors and has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. Its lead candidate, a monoclonal antibody for hepatitis delta, is being tested in clinical studies with the aim of functional cure.

about: Bright Peak Therapeutics is a Basel, Switzerland and San Diego biotech developing immunocytokines, targeted cytokine therapies that deliver IL-2 and other immune signals to tumours, for cancer immunotherapy. It is private and venture-backed, with a funding round in 2024. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. Founded in 2018 in Switzerland, it also has an office in San Diego, where parts of its research are located.

IDRx was a Cambridge, Massachusetts precision oncology biotech focused on gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST), developing next-generation KIT kinase inhibitors for patients who relapse on standard drugs. MBX Biosciences is a Carmel, Indiana biotech, listed on Nasdaq (MBX) since 2024, developing precision peptide therapies for endocrine and metabolic disorders, including MBX 2109 for hypoparathyroidism and MBX 1416 for post-bariatric hypoglycaemia, using its Precision Endocrine Peptide platform. It has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile. Founded in 2018 by Richard DiMarchi, a former Eli Lilly scientist and Indiana University professor, it designs long-acting peptide drugs.

about: ProfoundBio was a Woodinville, Washington and Suzhou, China biotech developing next-generation antibody-drug conjugates for cancer, including rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S) for ovarian cancer. Its lead rinatabart sesutecan targets folate receptor alpha and was in Phase 2 trials in ovarian and endometrial cancer, with Genmab planning registrational studies.

Rallybio is a New Haven, Connecticut biotech, listed on Nasdaq (RLYB), developing treatments for rare diseases in fetal and neonatal health, including RLYB212 to prevent fetal and neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia and RLYB116 for complement-mediated disease. It has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. It was founded in 2018 by Martin Mackay, a former head of research at Alexion, and listed on Nasdaq in 2021.

Recipharm is a Stockholm-headquartered pharmaceutical contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO), producing medicines for drug owners with sterile, oral, inhaled and biologics capacity across Europe, the US and Asia. It was listed on Nasdaq Stockholm and taken private by EQT in 2021, and has about 9,000 staff. Customers include global pharma and biotech. B2B manufacturer with no consumer profile. It offers formulation, development and commercial manufacture, with inhalation and biologics sites across Sweden, France, the UK and India.

Seismic Therapeutic is a Watertown, Massachusetts biotech using machine learning to design biologic drugs for immune-mediated diseases, such as engineered enzymes and antibodies for autoimmune conditions. It is venture-backed and has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. It is based near Boston's biotech cluster and has described building drugs from engineered proteins to reduce disease-causing antibodies.

Halda Therapeutics is a New Haven, Connecticut biotech developing oral cancer drugs based on regulated induced proximity targeting chimeras (RIPTACs), which kill cancer cells selectively by exploiting differences between tumour and normal cells, led by prostate cancer candidates. Johnson & Johnson agreed to acquire it in 2025 for about 3.05 billion dollars. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile. Its technology was developed in research linked to Yale and Halda raised large financing rounds in 2023 and 2024.

HiBio, Human Immunology Biosciences, was a South San Francisco biotech developing immune-targeted therapies for immune-mediated diseases, such as selective antibodies that address autoimmune and inflammatory conditions. Its lead programme was felzartamab, an anti-CD38 antibody licensed from MorphoSys, for kidney disease and other autoimmune conditions.

ImCheck Therapeutics was a Marseille, France biotech developing antibodies that activate gamma delta T cells for cancer, with lead candidate ICT01 targeting BTN3A in blood cancers. ICT01 had Phase 1/2 trials in AML and solid tumours, and the company was founded in Marseille in 2015 by cancer researchers.

Iterum Therapeutics is a Dublin-based clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (ITRM), developing orally and intravenously administered sulopenem, a penem antibiotic approved in the US in 2024 as Orlynvah for uncomplicated urinary tract infections in women. MycoWorks is an Emeryville, California biomaterials company that grows Fine Mycelium into Reishi, a leather-like material for fashion and automotive uses, without animal hides or plastic, at a plant in South Carolina.
